error_note: A 45-minute post-CRH ACTH is a stimulated value; a low result means a blunted response by challenge-specific criteria, not a decreased baseline circulating ACTH.
A reticulin autoantibody is a specific antibody, not a measure of total immunoglobulin; the polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia of Gaucher disease has nothing to do with reticulin antibodies.
A normal cat dander IgE excludes only cat sensitisation; the term covers all animal danders (dog, horse, etc.), which this test does not assess.
A low urinary epithelial cell count is a normal finding with no pathological meaning; the urine abnormality in microscopic polyangiitis is hematuria and red cell casts, not few epithelial cells.
The disease is marked by urinary formiminoglutamate specifically; routing through generic aminoaciduria (75 diseases) on a nominal amino-acid identifier code loses the analyte that matters.
Hypertension is an occasional, secondary (Cushing-related) and highly nonspecific feature of Carney complex, and a blood pressure panel has no single high result.
Lactic acidemia is characteristic of pyruvate carboxylase deficiency, but this is an unspecified-challenge (XXX) 30-minute code for which high is not defined as for baseline lactate.

The disease record excludes abnormal immunoglobulin levels (0%), yet a positive association was emitted; in addition a low Ascaris-specific IgE fraction is neither a total immunoglobulin measure nor pathological.

Thrombocytopenia is annotated as very rare in this disease and is shared by over 400 diseases, so the link carries little information (the very-rare frequency itself looks low for a marrow failure syndrome).
Hematocrit of pleural fluid assesses hemothorax, not circulating red cell mass; increased hematocrit in erythrocytosis refers to blood.
A normal C-peptide 1.5 hours after a glucose load is a stimulated value and cannot exclude an abnormal fasting or otherwise-timed C-peptide concentration.
Thrombocytopenia is a recognised severity criterion in preeclampsia (so the very-rare frequency is understated), but it affects a minority and is shared by hundreds of diseases.
Ectopic ACTH secretion from a gastric neuroendocrine neoplasm is a very rare occurrence, so a high ACTH says little about this disease.

Hypoglycemia is a very rare feature of histiocytoid cardiomyopathy, and a low glucose 4 hours after a glucose load reflects reactive hypoglycemia rather than the fasting hypoglycemia meant by the phenotype.
Erythropoietin concentration is a hormone level and does not show erythrocyte morphology; it has no recognised bearing on autoerythrocyte sensitization syndrome.
Raised testosterone is a very rare feature of polyembryoma, and the free-to-total testosterone ratio is not the serum testosterone level the phenotype names.

Ceruloplasmin is a copper-carrying protein, not copper itself; high ceruloplasmin (acute phase, estrogen) usually goes with raised total copper but the proper target is an increased ceruloplasmin term, not a nondirectional copper term.
Oxygen saturation plateaus at about 100% and cannot be meaningfully high; hyperoxemia is defined by an elevated arterial oxygen partial pressure, which saturation does not show.
A negative four-fruit mix screen says little about the whole class of plant-based food allergens (nuts, wheat, soy and others are untested), so it argues against the phenotype only marginally.
An unspecified-challenge (XXX) 30-minute LH has no defined low; a blunted stimulated response is not the same as a decreased baseline circulating LH.

A single-frequency, single-ear threshold (1000 Hz, left) stands in for full pure-tone audiometry of a high-frequency-predominant loss, and audiometry documents the hearing phenotype rather than diagnosing the DFNA25 entity.
Audiometry documents the sensorineural hearing loss but cannot diagnose this specific genetic subtype, which is established molecularly; it is a phenotyping test labelled diagnostic.
A single-frequency, single-ear threshold (2000 Hz, left) stands in for full audiometry, and audiometry documents deafness rather than diagnosing the DFNB102 genetic entity.
A reactive anti-HCV is a screening result showing past or present exposure; a quarter to a third of reactive people have cleared the virus, so current infection needs HCV RNA.

LDL-C of 190 mg/dL or more raises the probability of familial hypercholesterolemia but most such people have polygenic or secondary hypercholesterolemia; a risk marker is stated as indicating the disease.

The target is generic poisoning rather than lithium toxicity, and the TOXIC band uses EXTRIP dialysis-decision thresholds (4-5 mmol/L) although lithium toxicity begins around 1.5 mmol/L, so most toxic results fall outside the band.
The statement is a non-claim built on panic limits; it is true only as a schema placeholder, since much of 66-199 g/L (for example 70 g/L) is plainly abnormal for any adult.
An elevated TSH alone cannot show compensated (subclinical) hypothyroidism, which also requires a normal free T4; the same result occurs in overt hypothyroidism.
